reviews.reviewDescription: I bought two of these and they both lasted about a month before it became too difficult to turn them on. These are one of those lighting products where the "switch" is a tiny black nub that becomes harder and harder to twist, due to some trick of the manufacturer, so that after a few weeks you need a pair of vice grips to turn it on. Either that or your fingers get all bruised. I'm leaving this review so that Jeff Bezos knows that he basically needs to send me a new lamp every month until he can figure out how to fix this product. I didn't realize that I was purchasing a subscription, but I guess that's how it is. The metal is also very flimsy. Or he could go to jail, I'm not sure what the future holds for either of us. I'm pretty sure that this product is an illegal copy of a version that had been produced more honestly in the past. Everything about it is designed to be frustrating to the user. The adjustment knobs are incapable of tightening properly, by design. They do not grip, there are only 2 layers. You set the lamp up and watch it slowly sag like a sad tomato. Every time. When you move it the base threatens to break off, the metal that supports it is so weak. Whoever designed this lamp, clearly wanted to send a message that Americans should not be architects or try to do anything creative at a desk. If televisions were designed this badly, they would catch fire as soon as you plugged them in. A lamp is not rocket science. The only science here is the science of deliberately undermining usability for the consumer, while deceiving them into thinking they are getting a different product. I was able to purchase an "Ace Clamp Lamp" for $20 at the local Ace Hardware (see photo). It comes with a clip which is sufficiently strong to attach it to the edge of a book case, or to a door. The on-off switch is easy to operate, and doesn't bruise the fingers. You push it one way for "on" and the opposite way for "off", which is way simpler than having to turn a tiny slippery stuck knob, as you do with this product (and to have to turn it an even number of times for "stay the same" and an odd number of times for "change"). The angle can be adjusted easily using a ball clamp that always stays put when tightened. It never sags like a sad tomato, which incidentally makes me feel a lot safer with regards to fire danger. It is light-weight. It can take a 150 W bulb, not that you can buy those anymore. The only drawback is that you need another piece of furniture to attach it to; but that's way preferable to owning an appliance that was designed by your enemies to mock you.
reviews.author: AEAYFGEVLJZH4RVOZP63LA77LFDA

reviews.reviewDescription: This Artisians lamp is quite adequate if you can tighten the knobs enough to control it. It was easy to assemble and and the clamp seems very stable with a non-slip pad. The head does not rotate to point at the ceiling, which I enjoyed with my old lamp when I didn't want light in my eyes. This lamp covers several areas in my room, and works well.
reviews.author: AGKRDA3LGTNJXWS5VPR2PYQLNWSA

reviews.reviewDescription: I didn’t have much expectation for this lamp given the price point but it turned out to be pretty good. Light but solid if you tighten the nuts a bit and it serves the purpose. The only thing that can be improved is that it is way too loose in this socket so it rotates rather eagerly and if your desk is a bit tilted - it would be a problem. But this can be solved by wrapping the joint with some tape. What I value in this lamp is that I can use any bulb I want (that was the reason I bought it)
reviews.author: AELQ35KUEKHLVX53T5MFCYH536XA
